items.headline: Oracle drops Wisconsin lawsuit challenging data-center credit-rating rules
items.note: Oracle backs off a fight over state rules requiring credit-rating disclosures from data-center developers, an early sign regulators are pricing developer credit risk directly into build-out approvals.

items.headline: Bond traders flag $70B of 'shadow' credit backstops Nvidia and Broadcom extend to AI buildouts
items.note: Off-balance-sheet residual-value guarantees from Nvidia and Broadcom on AI debt deals aren't yet drawn, but rating agencies won't rule out being called on them in a downturn, understating true chipmaker leverage.

items.headline: BofA cuts Broadcom's credit outlook to Marketweight on hidden leverage in its XPV financing platform
items.note: Sell-side credit downgrade tied directly to the Blackstone/Apollo-backed XPV SPV, which could carry up to $370B in senior debt and exposes Broadcom to residual-value guarantees as large as $42B in stress scenarios.

items.headline: CoreWeave's backlog grows to $129B, but CDS still price a 50% five-year default probability
items.note: Credit markets keep pricing CoreWeave at distressed levels even after strong backlog growth, showing revenue momentum alone isn't resolving lenders' concerns about its GPU-debt load.

items.headline: Oracle's 5-year CDS hits record ~215bps as Apollo's Slok warns AI capex could 'self-throttle'
items.note: Oracle's default-insurance cost, up from ~145bps at year-end, is now the widest among major AI infrastructure names, with Apollo's chief economist flagging that rising all-in yields could force hyperscalers to throttle the capex cycle.

items.headline: CMBS investors push back as AI-linked data-center debt spreads widen
items.note: Two of the last three data-center-backed CMBS deals (CyrusOne, QTS) had to widen pricing to clear, a concrete sign of rising risk premiums in securitized AI infrastructure debt.

items.headline: AI loan investors demand covenants after CoreWeave's leveraged-loan spread blows out 125bps
items.note: Lenders forced CoreWeave to sweeten terms on a $2.6B facility, concrete evidence private credit is repricing AI/GPU-backed loan risk upward rather than just commentary.

items.headline: S&P downgrades Oracle to BBB-, one notch above junk, on AI-driven cash burn
items.note: Realized rating action: Oracle cut to the lowest investment-grade rung as its AI data-center buildout drives an estimated $42B free-cash-flow deficit, the clearest credit-event anchor in this cycle.
